Not a subclass of TextualRepresentation, and not an evidence source by classification: it is evidence when an isEvidenceFor assertion or a ValueEvidenceAnnotation says so. Disjoint with information content entity (D-011): a span may be designated by a selector, but a span that is asserted to be about or to designate something makes the data inconsistent."@en
<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextSpan> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#disjointWith> <https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000958>

CCO subtypes information content entities by what they are about; a representation is individuated by its exact sequence, a level CCO's information model has no class for, so it is placed directly under BFO generically dependent continuant. CCO defines information content entity as equivalent to a generically dependent continuant that is about some entity, and this class is disjoint with information content entity (D-011): asserting that a representation is about something, through cco:is about or any subproperty such as designates or describes, makes the data inconsistent. Relate a representation to what it expresses through a content-level information content entity instead."@en
<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-core#TextualRepresentation> <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#disjointWith> <https://www.commoncoreontologies.org/ont00000958>

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#AchievementDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Power under self-enhancement. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#AchievementDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A student's standing inclination to take the harder course because doing well in it is recognized as a sign of ability."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#BenevolenceDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Universalism under self-transcendence. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#BenevolenceDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to set aside their own plans to help a sibling or a close friend in difficulty."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#ConformityDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Tradition and Security under conservation. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#ConformityDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to hold back a sharp remark in a meeting so as not to upset colleagues."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#HedonismDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to choose a long, enjoyable meal with friends over an evening of extra work."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#PowerDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Achievement under self-enhancement. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#PowerDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to seek positions that bring authority over budgets and staff."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#SecurityDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Conformity and Tradition under conservation. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#SecurityDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to choose a stable job over a better-paid uncertain one, and to keep savings against emergencies."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#SelfDirectionDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Stimulation under openness to change. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#SelfDirectionDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to work out their own view of a problem rather than adopt the accepted one."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#StimulationDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Self-Direction under openness to change. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#StimulationDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to take up activities they have never tried, such as a sport with real risk or a sudden move to another country."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#TraditionDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Conformity and Security under conservation. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#TraditionDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to keep the family and religious customs they were raised in, such as observing holy days."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#UniversalismDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "One of the ten basic values of Schwartz's theory, grouped with Benevolence under self-transcendence. <https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-schwartz-values#UniversalismDisposition> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "A person's standing inclination to support protecting strangers and the natural environment even at a cost to themselves."@en

<https://fandaws.com/ontology/bfo/valuenet-moral-epistemics#AgentBehaviorProcess> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#example> "Agent C repeatedly ignoring a stated household rule."@en
